div.l: But natheles while I haue tyme and spase
Er that I ferther in this tale pace
Me thynketh it accordith on to raysoun
To telle yow of alle here condysyoun
Of eche of hem as it semed me
And which they were and of what degre
And eke what aray they were Inne
And at a knyht than wol I first bigynne
A Knyht ther was and that a wurthy man
That fro the tyme · that he first bigan
To rydyn out / he loved cheualrye
Trewthe and honour / fredom and courteysye
Wel worthy was he in his lordys werre
And ther hadde ryden / no man so ferre
As wel in crystendom as in hethnesse
And euyr honoured / for his worthynesse
At alisaundre he was / whan it was wonne
Wol ofte he hadde / the boord bigonne
A bouen alle naciōmns / in pruce
In lettowe hadde he reysed and in Ruce
No cristene man / so ofte of his degre
In gernade at the sege eek hadde he be
Of Algizir / and riden in belmarie
At lyeyes was he / and at Satalye
Whan they were wonne / and in the grete se
At many a noble / arme hadde he be
At mortel batayllys / hadde he befyftene
And fowhten / for owre feyth at Tramissene
In lyhstys thryes / and ay slayn his foo
This ilke wurthi knyht / hadde ben aso
Som tyme / with the lord of palatye
Ayen a nother / hethene in Turkye
And evirmore / he hadde a souereyne prys
And ther to eek / he worthy was and wys
And of his port / as meke as any mayde
